💡 Key Takeaways

  • While new United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is right now focused on getting United out of the relegation zone, he’ll also want to keep an eye on their loanees.
  • We’ve taken a look at every player that United sent out on loan in the summer and how they’ve performed this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have endured a disastrous start to the 2026-27 season, but how have their loanees fared away from the club?

While new United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is right now focused on getting United out of the relegation zone, he’ll also want to keep an eye on their loanees.

We’ve taken a look at every player that United sent out on loan in the summer and how they’ve performed this season.

The most high-profile player on this list, Onana spent two error-strewn years at Old Trafford before joining Trabzonspor on loan in 2025.

He helped them win the Turkish Cup last season, and they paid a fee in the region of £1million to bring him back to the club for a second loan spell.

The Cameroon international has kept seven clean sheets in 12 appearances in the Turkish Super League this season, and they currently have the best defensive record in the top flight.

He did concede from a corner in a Conference League group stage clash against Finnish side Kuopion Palloseura, but made amends by saving a penalty later in the game.

Karl Darlow’s arrival saw Bayindir deemed surplus to requirements at United, and he joined Celta Vigo on a season-long loan deal.

But the goalkeeper is yet to make a single appearance in LaLiga, as Romanian shot-stopper Ionut Radu is Celta’s clear No. 1.

He has also remained an unused substitute in the Europa League, and his only appearance to date came in a 5-0 win over fourth-tier side Salamanca CF in the Copa del Rey.

Reports in Spain suggest that Celta could look to terminate the loan deal in the January transfer window.

Harrison won the Denzil Haroun Reserve-Team Player of the Year award in the 2023-24 season, before going on loan to Chester and Shrewsbury Town.

The goalkeeper is now on his third temporary spell away from Old Trafford, having joined Scottish Championship club Greenock Morton in the summer.

He endured a difficult start to the season and lost six of his first seven games for the club, but has helped turn their form around in recent weeks.

The fourth goalkeeper on this list, Honor joined United from Blackburn Rovers earlier this year and initially linked up with their Under-21 squad.

He completed a loan move to National League North side Southport in the summer and started the first seven games of the season.

But the 20-year-old was dropped from the team after they signed fellow goalkeeper Douglass Lukjanciks on loan from Everton at the start of September.

He has been training at Carrington in recent weeks, and United could look to send him to another club once the January transfer window opens.

Kone spent the second half of last season on loan at Swiss Super League side Lausanne-Sport, who are also owned by Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Group.

The midfielder only made five appearances in an injury-hit spell, but returned to the club in the summer on a season-long loan deal.

He marked his first start of the season with an assist against Young Boys, and followed that up with a goal and an assist in a 6-0 win in the Swiss Cup.

But the 20-year-old was shown a straight red card in a 4-0 defeat against Lugano in September and has since made just two substitute appearances.

After winning the Rotherham United Player of the Season award in 2025-26, Gore returned to League One and joined Luton Town on a season-long loan deal.

An injury disrupted his bright start to the season at Kenilworth Road, but he has found his way back into the team in recent matches.

“He’s done really well Dan, and it was a shame he picked up a slight injury which was a strange one,” Luton manager Jack Wilshere said.

“He just slipped in training and then he was out for two weeks. It kind of killed his rhythm a little bit. He came on the pitch against Colchester and he was one of the real positives from that game as he was slowly, slowly building, so we have to get him back to that place.

According to recent reports, “I thought he was good, he’s aggressive, he’s tenacious in midfield. He uses the ball well, he can drive the game forward and someone we’re going to need.”.

The 22-year-old midfielder helped Luton book a place in the FA Cup second round by registering an assist against Forest Green Rovers.

Following their success with Gore, Rotherham United went shopping at Old Trafford again and signed Fitzgerald on a season-long loan deal.

The midfielder is being managed by Alex Bruce, who also came through the United academy and is the son of three-time Premier League winner Steve Bruce.

He was initially eased into the team at the start of the season, but has now established himself as one of the first names on the teamsheet.

The 19-year-old has picked up multiple Man of the Match awards and was named their Player of the Month for October after registering two assists.

“I felt Jayce (Fitzgerald) was outstanding again and what a prospect he is,” Bruce said after a 0-0 draw with Grimsby Town.

Moorhouse had interest from Plymouth, Huddersfield, Wigan and Stockport in the summer before joining Dundee United on a season-long loan deal.

The midfielder made just two appearances in the Scottish Premiership before sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury in a friendly.

He has returned to United and is now set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

After spending the second half of last season on loan at St Mirren, Devaney returned to Scotland and joined Hibernian.

The loan deal also includes an option to make the move permanent at the end of the season, although he is still hoping for a future at Old Trafford.

According to recent reports, “I’ve experienced that a lot in the short career that I’ve had so far,” he said. “But, as I said, I’ll back myself to go in at United at the start of next season and impress.”.

He started their first four games of the season but came off the bench against Dundee United and was sent off just six minutes later for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.

In the process, the 19-year-old suffered an ankle injury that kept him on the sidelines for a month, and he has only just returned.

He will hope to be back in the starting line-up by the time Hibernian face Rangers in the Scottish League Cup final next month.

Wheatley was linked with a permanent move to Everton in the summer, but United ultimately decided to send him on loan to Championship side Lincoln City.

The striker made his debut off the bench in a Carabao Cup tie against Blackpool, but then picked up an injury that put him on the sidelines.

He recently returned to full fitness and made his Championship debut, playing 59 minutes in a 1-0 defeat at home to Wrexham.

“There were some flashes of what he’s capable of,” head coach Tom Shaw said. “Ethan, obviously that’s his first start, he’s not had loads of football, but he’s a high-potential young player. He’s got good athleticism, good quality.

Sources indicate that “Perhaps he didn’t have enough of those moments and situations to show that today, but we know that the threat is there. That’ll be really good for him, the 60 minutes and the experience.”.

Having starred for Arsenal’s academy, Chido Obi arrived at United in 2024 with a reputation as one of football’s most exciting young talents.

The striker made eight first-team appearances in his debut season, but remained with United’s youth sides throughout the 2025-26 campaign.

He joined newly-promoted Eredivisie side Willem II in the summer in search of regular first-team football, but the loan move has not gone to strategy.

The 18-year-old has no goals to his name and is yet to start a single game for the club, with all seven of his appearances to date coming off the substitutes’ bench.

He also faced criticism for his lack of defensive work after Willem II went down to 10 men in a domestic cup win over Helmond Sport.

“It is partly a matter of mindset, but also of youthful exuberance,” then-caretaker manager Adrie Koster said. “That boy has never experienced anything like this before.

Sources indicate that “He doesn’t do it on purpose either, so we shouldn’t focus everything on him. This is simply part of his learning process. But we are going to talk to him about it.”.

United are set to consider recalling the Denmark Under-21 international in the January transfer window.

#163265. AI is ditching hallucinated references — and other bad habits

AI is ditching hallucinated references — and other bad habits

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that hallucinated academic citations have become a hallmark of the artificial-intelligence era.
  • Recent findings suggest that the finding is part of an analysis that reports that many LLM tendencies, such as overthinking simple mathematics problems and complying with illogical requests, fade over time as AI companies release new or updated models with improved capabilities.
  • “We, as consumers of these systems, need to not have such a fixed view of what AI can do and what it can’t do,” states co-author Owen Queen, an AI researcher at Stanford University in California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: FabrikaSimf/Shutterstock.

Recent findings suggest that hallucinated academic citations have become a hallmark of the artificial-intelligence era. But they might soon be gone for good. Researchers have found that the latest large language models (LLMs) rarely, if ever, attribute information to sources that don’t exist.

Recent findings suggest that the finding is part of an analysis that reports that many LLM tendencies, such as overthinking simple mathematics problems and complying with illogical requests, fade over time as AI companies release new or updated models with improved capabilities. Many of these tendencies disappear about 16 months after the phenomenon is first described in a published paper. The analysis, described in a blogpost, has not been peer reviewed.

“We, as consumers of these systems, need to not have such a fixed view of what AI can do and what it can’t do,” states co-author Owen Queen, an AI researcher at Stanford University in California.

But just because an LLM behaviour fades as models improve doesn’t mean that the effect immediately disappears, says Maxim Topaz, a health-care AI researcher at Columbia University in Fresh York City. Topaz has found1 that the number of hallucinated citations in academic papers has risen drastically since 2023, probably because more researchers than ever before are using LLMs, and they often aren’t using the latest models.

It has been revealed that queen and his colleague identified 50 widely cited LLM behaviours that were described in publications between late 2022, when some of the first LLMs became widely available, and late 2025. They then gave the same prompts that first elicited the behaviour in the original publications to 20 LLMs that were released from mid-2024 to late 2026 to see if the effect has strengthened or weakened over time. For example, they asked each model to count the number of r’s in ‘strawberry’ — something that LLMs have found difficult but can now do more reliably.

Nearly half of the behaviours they checked have largely disappeared from newer models, leading the researchers to deem those effects ‘expired’. Expired behaviours had an average lifespan of about 16 months after publication, although some were fleeting — models stopped overthinking simple maths problems just a month and a half after this tendency was published. Other traits persisted, such as the stereotyping of Black women by disproportionately describing them as resilient, which lasted for longer than three years.

Industry observers note that although most of the retested LLM behaviours have faded over time, three have become more pronounced. Today’s models praise what their people like even more often than they used to, LLMs favour their own writing more strongly than that of other LLMs and people; and LLMs are now even worse than they used to be at generating truly random numbers.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03753-1.

Topaz, M., Roguin, N., Gupta, P., Zhanga, Z. & Peltonen, L.-M. Lancet 407, 1779–1781 (2026).

Roma continues to monitor the attacking market ahead of the winter transfer window, evaluating various opportunities to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attack.

Following rumors of interest in Endrick, another name has emerged that could fuel competition with AC Milan: Fotis Ioannidis, a 2000-born Greek striker at the moment playing for Sporting CP.

AC Milan is closely monitoring Ioannidis in their search for a centre-forward to replace Camarda, including the Greek among the options being evaluated along with Endrick and Tresoldi.

One potential player who could influence AC Milan’s interest is Ruben Amorim, who has previously worked with the striker at Sporting CP and knows his characteristics.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Roma considers the player an interesting prospect, although they haven’t identified him as a top priority.

The European calendar will soon offer the Giallorossi the opportunity to observe the striker firsthand. On December 8th, Ioannidis will face Roma in the Champions League for Sporting CP, a match that could be an vital opportunity to assess his qualities.

So far, the Greek has made 15 appearances this season, scoring two goals and providing two assists.

Industry observers note that gasperini, however, is primarily looking for a winger with acceleration, the ability to beat his man, and the ability to attack space—characteristics different from those of a central striker like the Greek. Therefore, any further exploration of Ioannidis will also depend on the opportunities that arise during the January transfer window.

Why electrification is the climate game changer we need

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas.
  • If fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels.
  • Sources indicate that in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas. Which also means significantly slashing the heat-trapping CO2 emissions that are linked to flooding and extreme heat around the world.

If fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels. That is according to a recent analysis by the International Energy Agency, which also found that such an acceleration could mean the world needs 18 million fewer barrels of oil per day.

Sources indicate that in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives. That means switching from diesel cars to electric vehicles (EVs), turning off gas heating and using electricity to power heat pumps.

Industry observers note that but the way the electricity running these things is generated is also vital. In theory, an EV using power created in a coal-heavy electricity grid could be worse for the climate than a car running on gas.

Electricity derived from renewable energy sources such as solar, wind or hydropower on the other hand produces clean power.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the booming EV market is the fastest-growing electrification sector. Globally, one in four cars sold in 2025 was electric and since 2020, international sales have increased by almost 600%.

Nonetheless, electricity only covers about 20% of final energy use in the wider global economy, including that used in businesses, factories and people's homes.

It would need to supply more than half of all power by 2050 if we are to avoid runaway heating and the more intense and extreme weather events connected to a hotter climate.

Some industries and activities are harder to electrify than others. While it's relatively easy to switch to EVs and decarbonize buildings, some industries such as petrochemicals and steel use fossil fuels as raw materials to make products like plastics, fertilizer, detergent or steel.

In addition, while heat pumps work well for low-temperature needs, they can't replace the temperatures needed in steelmaking or cement production.

The World Resources Institute, an independent research organization, recommends hydrogen, synthetic fuels or other low-carbon alternatives as more viable options than electrification in cases such as ocean shipping and aviation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In addition to cutting down on greenhouse gas emissions resulting in cleaner air and limiting global heating, electrification is also more efficient and cheaper in the long run.

A combustion engine in a car wastes as much as 80% of its fuel energy, mostly to turn it into heat. Only about 20% is converted to actually move the car. Electric motors, on the other hand, convert about 80% of electrical energy into motion.

Sources indicate that as the World Resources Institute points out, running all appliances on electricity will increase electricity consumption. Yet total energy costs are likely to be lower, even if electricity becomes more expensive.

It has been revealed that as electricity needs grow due to the rapid expansion of AI, data centers and the overall shift to a more electrified world, outpaced grids struggle to keep up. This is increasingly holding back the energy transition, delaying the rollout of additional renewable generation, storage capacity and electrified demand.

According to the International Energy Agency, annual grid investment has to increase by about 50% by 2030 from today's $400 billion.

There's also a major mismatch between how long it takes to set up newly introduced grid infrastructure (five to 15 years), compared to renewable energy projects (one to five years), and EV charging infrastructure (one to two years).

Experts say we need smarter grids that support a two-way flow of electricity while remaining secure, stable and able to keep up with higher demand as electrification intensifies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026.

This is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth. Will they ever stop winning? Will Evanilson ever stop scoring?

The numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

In a recent development, this is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

It has been revealed that make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

It has been revealed that they move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

‘We never really struggled, said Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions.

Sources indicate that 'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I mentioned, this is a tough job.

According to recent reports, ‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'.

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

Industry observers note that rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

His opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

In a recent development, that’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match.

Forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

It has been revealed that the visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

In a recent development, ’The defeat was deserved,’ stated Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

According to recent reports, 'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’.

Sources indicate that when asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'.

Did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break.

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form.

In a recent development, bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

His superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ mentioned Rose.

Sources indicate that ‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'.

James Tarkowski picked up the first red of his Premier League career on Monday night and let’s be honest, we all thought he had more than that.

Tarkowski was shown the red for the follow-through on a tackle on Brentford’s Yehor Yarmolyuk which saw his name crossed off a list of players who have surprisingly never received a red.

Here are the remaining candidates:.

A career of 323 games and not a single red card is an impressive feat from King.

The former Tottenham defender’s struggles with injuries are well known with him only twice playing more than 30 Premier League games in a single season but when he was on the pitch, he was as composed as can be.

Not only did King never get his marching orders, he only got nine yellows in every match he played.

King’s numbers are impressive, but the record belongs to Hughes.

The former Newcastle, Fulham and Aston Villa man played 455 Premier League matches but never received a red card.

In total, the Northern Irishman played 675 games in his career and was never sent off, earning 19 yellows in that time.

Considering how composed he often looked, perhaps we could not be too surprised that Lahm features on this list.

He played in eight different positions in his career but never once was so out of his depth that he got himself sent off.

Lahm primarily operated as a full-back with 269 appearances on the right and 219 on the left before Pep Guardiola converted him into a defensive midfielder.

He did quite like a yellow though, getting 49 in his career.

Considering he played the majority of his career as a sweeper, it is particularly impressive that Italian legend Scirea was never sent off.

The World Cup and European Cup-winning defender played 621 times and yet was never given his marching orders.

To make it even more impressive, in his long career, which featured 551 games for Juventus, Scirea got just four yellow cards.

The former Match of the Day host is well known for having not only never received a red, but never even got booked either.

Lineker played 468 games, the majority of which were in the First Division, and yes he was a striker but we could show you a long list of number nines who have picked up a red.

The closest Lineker ever came was in Euro 1992 when he stamped on Basile Boli’s toe. The ref missed it and the pre-VAR world meant Lineker was in the clear.

Not only did Barnes never receive a red, but he was also the first player to make it past 100 Premier League games without a card of either colour.

Barnes played most of his football pre-Premier League, getting 349 appearances in the old First Division before making 201 in the Premier League, but never got a red.

He ended his career with 696 games played and not a single entry in the referee’s book.

Sources indicate that iniesta getting a red card just feels wrong, doesn’t it? Well, the good news is it’s never happened.

Iniesta played 885 games in his career, 674 of which were for Barcelona, but never received a red card.

He did pick up a fair few yellows, having got 74 in his time.

Considering he was quite a robust winger, Duff being on this list is surprising.

He played 629 games, starting off with Blackburn before moving to Chelsea in 2003, yet never got a red card.

Instead, he got 42 yellows, the majority of which came with Rovers, but he was largely a clean player.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

O’Neill said: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’.

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic.

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill noted: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’.

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I thought he did very well,’ remarked O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’.

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ remarked McLeish.

In a recent development, ‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’.

The making of O Fenomeno: How Ronaldo became a global superstar at PSV

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How do you even begin to choose your favourite version of Ronaldo Nazario?
  • Recent findings suggest that the prodigy at Cruzeiro?
  • He even had his moments in a brief, mostly forgettable stint at AC Milan before rounding out his career with yet more silverware at Corinthians.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How do you even begin to choose your favourite version of Ronaldo Nazario?

Recent findings suggest that the prodigy at Cruzeiro? The unstoppable force of nature at Bobby Robson’s Barcelona? The Galactico at Real Madrid? The heartbreak of France 98, the glorious redemption of the 2002 World Cup or the pre-injury sensation at Inter, when he looked destined to become the greatest striker of all time?

He even had his moments in a brief, mostly forgettable stint at AC Milan before rounding out his career with yet more silverware at Corinthians.

It has been revealed that over time, Ronaldo’s physique famously changed dramatically, his game evolved and the freakish acceleration that once made him impossible to catch was compromised by injuries. He suffered serious knee injuries, underwent multiple operations and had to rebuild his career more than once.

Sources indicate that younger generations can spend hours watching Ronaldo highlights on YouTube and still miss something fundamental about his greatness. The goals, the skills and the trademark explosive bursts are all there, but clips can’t capture the resilience that became such a defining part of his legend.

Kylian Mbappe is the obvious modern reference point, stylistically speaking: no other player is blessed with that devastating combination of pace, dynamism and finishing.

But mercifully, the French superstar has been spared the harrowing injuries that repeatedly threatened Ronaldo’s career. Mbappe is yet to experience the extraordinary highs and lows, the adversity and the comebacks, that made Ronaldo’s story so compelling.

In many ways, you can trace the whole arc of Ronaldo’s career back to his two seasons with PSV.

The jaw-dropping athleticism, the insane rate of goalscoring, the sense that defenders were powerless to stop him – it was all there for a teenager in his first stint in Europe. So, too, was the first major injury setback, the beginning of a long and painful relationship with the treatment table.

Ronaldo arrived in Eindhoven in 1994 as a 17-year-old, fresh from being part of Brazil’s World Cup-winning squad, albeit without playing a minute.

It might seem an unlikely destination for South America’s hottest prospect, but the European football landscape was unrecognisable if you view it through a modern lens.

This was an era in which arguably the best forward in the world – Romario – had stayed in Eindhoven for five full seasons. Meanwhile, over in Amsterdam, Louis van Gaal was building the best team on the planet. Ajax won the Champions League in 1994-95; Ronaldo’s PSV were competing with one of the great teams of that era.

Ajax were the dominant force in Dutch football, built around an outstanding collective rather than one superstar. They had exceptional players, of course, but nobody quite like Ronaldo.

The teenager hit the ground running at PSV, scoring one and setting up another on his Eredivisie debut before proceeding to take the league by storm.

According to recent reports, PSV were a different proposition altogether. They lacked their great rivals’ cohesion and tactical sophistication, and they made a chaotic start to that campaign.

A hat-trick from Ronaldo couldn’t prevent PSV from losing 5-4 to Bayer Leverkusen in an early-season UEFA Cup qualifier; an apt reflection of where that team was at.

“The Ronaldo show started, and he scored three goals,” former PSV Technical Director Frank Arnesen later told Mundial.

Recent findings suggest that “But it wasn’t about the goals even; there was one detail in the game that was incredible. He received the ball in his own half. The ball is played to him, and the German right back assaults him from behind in a dangerous way.

Sources indicate that “He lifts the ball with the outside of his left shoe, around the defender, and jumps. Ronaldo passes him by on the other side and starts a solo. He moves past three or four men, one man two times. Then all of Europe knew about Ronaldo.”.

﻿.

It has been revealed that while Ronaldo was swiftly establishing himself as the most exciting talent of his generation, PSV were struggling to keep pace. Manager Aad de Mos had bafflingly deployed centre-forward Erik Meijer at left-back in the defeat to Leverkusen and departed in October.

Kees Rijvers stepped in on a caretaker basis before Dick Advocaat was eventually appointed in December, making for a turbulent introduction to life in Europe.

The Farmers – the club’s nickname, but not an entirely unfair reflection of their level – finished third, behind Roda JC and a full 14 points adrift of Van Gaal’s unbeaten Ajax side in 1994-95.

It has been revealed that that gap would have been even greater under the three-points-for-a-win system. Still, in an otherwise struggling PSV side, Ronaldo was a class apart, claiming the Golden Boot with 30 Eredivisie goals – 12 more than his nearest challenger, fellow wonderkid Patrick Kluivert.

The buck-toothed teenager was doing that all that while adapting to life on a latest continent, experiencing the culture shock of his first winter in the chilly, damp industrial heartland of the Netherlands.

It was there and then that he learned to drive, with his instructor recalling him in the glowing tones of a proud youth coach speaking to The Athletic for a long read.

“His driving skills were excellent, of course, but his scanning, his awareness of his surroundings, and his anticipation, the things we actually train for, were far from elite-level,” John Dekker told Dutch outlet omroepbrabant, with a nod to his student’s newfound celebrity status.

“It was incredible how swiftly people recognised him. People crowding around the car, girls sitting on the hood… it was great fun.”.

PSV were an entertaining side, but the real improvements came after a full pre-season under Advocaat. By the start of 1995-96, they looked a considerably more coherent outfit, with Ronaldo leading an increasingly formidable attack. They were routinely running riot domestically, putting four, five, seven and even eight goals past Eredivisie opponents.

@Inter_en @Ronaldo Sorry, but we’re not convinced 😜.

#PSVFCIM https://t.co/IVuyojH3Fe.

O Fenomeno looked set to go truly stratospheric when he scored four goals and set up another two as PSV demolished Finnish minnows MyPa 7-1, a performance that bordered on bullying.

It has been revealed that yet the Dutch side had plenty of other weapons. Ronaldo sat out their 5-3 win over Leeds at Elland Road and wasn’t among the scorers in the 3-0 home victory in the second leg. There was no repeat of the previous season’s debacle as they cruised through qualifying into the UEFA Cup proper.

But just as things were gathering pace, Ronaldo suffered his first major injury: a patellar tendon tear that kept him sidelined for almost the entire second half of the season, including a minor UEFA Cup classic against Barcelona. PSV gave the Catalans two terrific games but ultimately bowed out 5-4 on aggregate in the quarter-finals.

Recent findings suggest that who knows what Advocaat’s PSV might have gone on to achieve had they kept their one bonafide superstar fit and available? They finished runners-up that season, closing the gap to just six points on an Ajax side that Van Gaal had led to a second successive Champions League final.

Ronaldo returned towards the end of the campaign, but not without conflict. His relaxed Brazilian temperament didn’t always sit comfortably with Advocaat’s strict Dutch sensibilities, echoing the coach’s issues with Gullit. Ronaldo reportedly called his manager an “idiot” after being left out of the starting XI for the KNVB Cup final.

“Yes, he did say that,” Advocaat later confirmed.

Recent findings suggest that “Ronaldo was out injured for a long time in his second year. We used Rene Eijkelkamp in his place. When Ronaldo recovered, he demanded to start in the Cup final against Sparta. I didn’t want to take the risk, and he got very angry and said some harsh words. But we had no lasting problems.”.

“At times, I felt like a father to him. After away games, he’d fall asleep on the bus with his head resting on my shoulder. He was open and had his personal struggles, but to me, he was a sweet kid.”.

Ronaldo was introduced from the bench for a late cameo and promptly notched an assist, adding extra gloss to a 5-2 victory. He had his trophy, giving him a fitting send-off in his final appearance.

Industry observers note that there would be considerably more spectacular comebacks in the years ahead. While the knee injury was an early warning of what was to come, it hadn’t yet taken anything away from Ronaldo’s extraordinary physical gifts.

At Barcelona the following season, he reached arguably the highest level of his career, described by Spanish football lifer Sid Lowe as “quite possibly the best, most freakishly brilliant thing I have ever seen.”.

The 2002 World Cup is the obvious Oscar-bait centrepiece for a Ronaldo biopic. His PSV years would be the indie arthouse prequel: A human story of teenage brilliance, growing pains and the fighter behind the phenomenon. The connoisseur’s choice for a favourite Ronaldo chapter.

Breaking: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.
  • Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

"Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was launched.

"In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related challenges and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their problem is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club said "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

Industry observers note that this campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (SUBSTANTIAL) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

Sources indicate that "My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

Industry observers note that the fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's plan" and that homosexuality is a sin.

Borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Sources indicate that article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

In a recent development, the use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Big-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

And yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the newly introduced opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

Tech Report: Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr.
  • A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms.
  • Industry observers note that the findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr. Chris Henstridge/SPL.

A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms. Now, neuroscientists are discovering that the brain is the conductor of these responses — decoding the type of pathogen that has invaded, accessing memories of past bouts of illness and even mobilizing immune defences at the sight of a sick person.

Industry observers note that the findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell. Neuroscientists have long viewed neurological responses to infection as a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation, rather than a strategy tailored to the threat.

“Sickness is actually not a fixed program, although we often talk about it this way,” said Jessica Osterhout, a neurobiologist at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who chaired the session.

A bacterial infection and a cold caused by a virus can both result in fever and exhaustion, yet they rarely trigger the same constellation of symptoms. Bacterial infections, for instance, tend to suppress appetite much more sharply than do colds, which made Osterhout and her colleagues wonder how the brain tells various pathogens apart.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Sources indicate that in unpublished experiments, Osterhout’s team compared mice injected with a bacterial toxin with those given a compound that mimics a viral infection. To see how the brain distinguished between pathogens, the researchers profiled individual cells in circumventricular organs, which are specialized structures with unusually permeable blood vessels that surround brain ventricles.

When the body has an infection, cells in the circumventricular organs switch on sets of immune-related genes and release distinct mixes of chemical signals. Those signals diffuse to nearby neurons and create distinct patterns of activity for different pathogens, allowing the brain to customize its symptom profile depending on the threat.

Rather than acting as conduits that let inflammatory signals pass unchecked from the blood into the wider brain, these structures “may actually interpret them”, Osterhout mentioned.

Sometimes, the brain doesn’t even wait for pathogens to enter the body to rally the immune system1. Andrea Serino, a neuroscientist at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, studies how the brain maps peripersonal space, which is the area around the body roughly in arm’s reach.

It has been revealed that when Serino’s team placed volunteers in virtual reality, they found that threat-monitoring brain regions became active when avatars bearing skin lesions caused by viral or bacterial infections approached, even when the figures were beyond arm’s reach. Just 15 minutes of virtual exposure triggered a surge in frontline immune ‘sentinel’ cells in participants’ blood comparable to that induced by an influenza vaccine. This reaction did not occur when participants saw healthy-looking avatars or ones expressing fear.

These experiments suggest that the immune system uses “the predictive ability of the brain to react before pathogens enter the body”, Serino remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller firm she worked for.

Recent findings suggest that alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing company. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

It has been revealed that according to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the organization advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

This type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

In a recent development, at the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the company's website as of November 2026.

Sources indicate that "There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," it said. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.".

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the Newly introduced York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

Recent findings suggest that megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

According to recent reports, alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the company's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

According to recent reports, the Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

Industry observers note that alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

According to recent reports, in December 2025, Nvidia stated its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the manufacturer was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell company with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

According to recent reports, sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

It has been revealed that “I don’t know,” Sage mentioned when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

It has been revealed that “I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he stated. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

It has been revealed that “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

It has been revealed that “The first work to do is on me,” he noted. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

Industry observers note that “It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

Sources indicate that for all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage noted. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Recent findings suggest that three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

According to recent reports, “It’s not my decision,” Sage remarked. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really notable to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

It has been revealed that with only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Recent findings suggest that diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

It has been revealed that all Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

In a recent development, “In these moments it’s about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and being quick to go to the action was impressive.”.

The presence of mind to attempt something outlandish was one thing; the execution was quite another. With Benítez vulnerable, Gómez took just one touch with his right foot before taking his shot, not giving the keeper enough time to scramble back to cover his line. As he looked up to confirm the opportunity, the 23-year-old struck the ball over Benítez with such venom that it did not even bounce until it reached the goal.

All that remained was for the Paraguayan international to hurtle towards the corner flag, engulfed by his ecstatic team-mates. For the Brighton fans, soaked by showers at the Amex, rain can never have felt so sweet.

Industry observers note that gómez’s goal will earn comparisons with David Beckham’s lob from the halfway line at Wimbledon. The advancements in pressing and conditioning in the 30 years since, with space ever more congested, makes such a strike even harder today. Not since Wayne Rooney in 2017 has a player scored a Premier League goal from further out than Gómez’s 56 yards.

Gómez may well attempt an encore. He shot from even further out at the Stadium of Light a week ago. When October ends, three of the last four Premier League goal-of-the-month winners will be Brighton players. Alongside his meticulous emphasis on set-pieces, Hürzeler empowers flair in open play.

According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

According to recent reports, yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German stated: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

Recent findings suggest that in his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future

📖 0% read

  • It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception.
  • In a recent development, but when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's no secret that getting playing time is important to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

In a recent development, but when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

Sources indicate that "I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can.".

Sources indicate that A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

In a recent development, although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

In a recent development, the match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

At some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment.".

For now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned.
  • And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

It has been revealed that do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions, with a belligerence of their own, ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. Their mistake was in thinking it was dead.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.

By this point, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal were 1-0 in front. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

Industry observers note that ‘We were exceptional in the first half,’ he later mentioned. ‘We have won matches playing much worse than we did here. The intensity, the aggression – we should have been 3-0 or 4-0 up. But right from the start of the second half, we weren’t at the races. We lost duels, gave the ball away and gave them belief.’.

In a recent development, arteta had Noni Madueke to thank for rescuing the point. The winger was his best player throughout and, had he earlier shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

So dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more bloodthirst when on top.

Industry observers note that arteta, you feel, gets more of a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday.

‘The second half was pure belief, pure conviction, pure trust in the team-mate,’ mentioned Jaissle, under increased scrutiny amid the presence of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan.

According to recent reports, ‘There were so many ball-wins with a vertical approach and causing them problems. This is the Newcastle DNA.’.

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes - booed after each of his 36, ineffectual touches - was hooked in the 70th minute, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

The league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya that requires an MRI scan.

It has been revealed that the goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his shoulder, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders.

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained.

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured.

If Newcastle were to beat Arsenal, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast.

Sources indicate that at least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as the half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence.

Come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to.

Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End.

According to recent reports, newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90).

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret.

It has been revealed that the goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine.

The punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless. Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red.

So, it was as if two sides had swapped shirts after the break. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits.

Sources indicate that suddenly, they were able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive, they drew level just four minutes after the restart.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss.

The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend - Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

'We needed players with more energy and physicality,’ said Jaissle, explaining his half-time changes.

According to recent reports, ‘The tactics did not change, it was purely the front footed behaviour. Throw away the doubts, then you saw what is possible. We had Arsenal shaking. I hope we can carry on this feeling.’.

Newcastle looked the most likely winners until Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. Still, the hosts came back for more.

Industry observers note that arsenal had arrived intent on silencing St James’. In the end, they were grateful for the sound of the full-time whistle.

#163245. Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
