Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the latest campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Sources indicate that tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” mentioned Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

It has been revealed that kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:04 EST, 23 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his plans were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

Recent findings suggest that 'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he said, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

It has been revealed that 'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

And his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

It has been revealed that 'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

It has been revealed that 'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

In a recent development, 'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws.
  • Sources indicate that known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk.
  • Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws.

Sources indicate that known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk. The Polish prime minister pledged to introduce abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy before the 2023 parliamentary election, but his coalition has been unable to agree on a common position.

Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.

In Poland, abortion is only allowed when the pregnancy is the result of a crime — rape or incest — or when it endangers the health or life of the woman.

Justyna Wydrzynska, an activist from a nonprofit organization called Abortion Dream Team, demonstrated DW the "Abortomat" in a small room behind a tasseled portiere at Abotak, Poland's first abortion center.

Inside, the pink lighting is subdued. Glitter tassels, baubles and spotlights make it feel a bit like a disco, she said.

According to recent reports, the "Abortomat," which opened in late September, has 22 pink lockers. To open one, a woman receives a PIN code from the organization Women Help Women after completing a medical questionnaire, which is then checked by a doctor.

Parcel lockers have sprung up like mushrooms after rain in Poland in recent years. Even the smallest villages have them.

"When you walk around Poland, vending machines are everywhere. This is our culture. People in the US have Amazon, we have vending machines for everything," mentioned Wydrzynska.

In a recent development, women in Poland who have an abortion are not criminalized. But anyone who helps them terminate a pregnancy risks up to three years in prison.

According to recent reports, in 2023, Wydrzynska was the first activist to be convicted in Poland of helping a woman to have an abortion by sending her pills. The conviction was later overturned, and the court ordered a retrial.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Inside each compartment at the "Abortomat" is a package that normally contains two drugs, mifepristone and misoprostol, usually taken up to the 14th week of pregnancy.

Sources indicate that because mifepristone is not registered in Poland, the drug must be ordered from abroad where it is legal. Information on how to do this is not easy to come by, which is where Abortion Dream Team and Abotak come in. They help women find information about accessing medication, which is sent from abroad by Women Help Women, or help them to travel abroad for a termination.

Wydrzynska remarked she believes the "Abortomat" does not break the law because it is a machine, not a person, that is delivering the pills, although she admits she is not sure.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Sabrina Mana-Walasek, a reproductive rights lawyer representing Wydrzynska, remarked the legal environment for abortion pills is "complicated.".

She stated that although mifepristone is not registered in Poland, it is registered in the European Union and, as EU citizens, Polish women can order it and take it.

"If a woman orders pills for herself and pays for them herself, it's not a crime," she remarked.

The ultra-Catholic legal group Ordo Iuris disagrees and has notified the prosecutor's office that the activists are committing a crime.

"In the case of an 'Abortomat,' the actions enabling a woman to have an abortion are theoretically performed by the woman herself using the device, but the reality is that this machine is operated by people — they send the code required to open the compartment containing abortion pills, they order and procure the pills, and they restock the compartments," said Katarzyna Gesiak, director of the Ordo Iuris Center for Medical Law and Bioethics.

Wydrzynska remarked anti-abortion activists regularly demonstrate outside Abotak, using horns and loudspeakers to generate loud noise to annoy the center's residential neighbors and pressure the landlord to revoke their rental agreement.

At one demonstration, a woman holding an image of the Virgin Mary told DW she believes abortion "is the work of Satan.".

"Abortion is evil, it's demonic, it's against the fifth Commandment, 'Thou shalt not kill,'" she said.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, Diana, a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman living in Warsaw, used abortion pills during her sixth week of pregnancy before the "Abortomat" started up. She got the pills using information provided by Abortion Dream Team.

Diana told DW that she has never wanted to have children.

"I was expecting something like a headache, stomachache, maybe vomiting, but I had nothing like that. It was just like a normal period. I didn't feel any pain. It was really easy for me," she noted.

"I felt relief because I knew that it was the right choice for me. I knew that I can live my life," she added.

Another Abortion Dream Team activist, Natalia Broniarczyk, said they help about 130 women daily in Poland. About 125 of these women use pills that cost about €75 ($83), while the remainder travel to a clinic abroad.

In contrast, just 851 abortions were performed in Polish hospitals last year.

Broniarczyk is concerned about the rising support for right-wing parties ahead of next year's parliamentary election, but she's also furious at the inactivity of liberals in Tusk's coalition.

"I'm mad at the liberals because for three years, they did nothing to protect us. They lost three years and now, when we're close to an election, they are fighting for our voices and respect. People are more progressive than politicians," she noted.

After taking office in 2023, Tusk's coalition, which includes left-wing and conservative partners, were unable to agree a common position and their separate bills failed to obtain parliamentary approval in 2024.

Afterwards, Tusk stated abortion on request would not be possible during the current parliamentary term.

In October, however, two bills were resubmitted to the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, and were narrowly approved.

It has been revealed that one reinstates severe irreversible fetal defects as a justification for a legal termination. This justification had been ruled illegal by the Constitutional Court in 2020 when the previous right-wing Law and Justice (PiS)-led government was in power.

The 2020 ruling led to tens of thousands of people, mostly women, taking part in street protests in towns and cities across the country, some of the largest since communism fell in 1989.

Lawmakers also approved a bill partially decriminalizing anyone who helps a woman terminate her pregnancy.

According to the results of a recent poll conducted by SW Research for Onet.pl, almost 61% of respondents remarked they want the country's right-wing president, Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, to sign into law the bill on the fetal defect justification.

Nawrocki opposes abortion, and both Wydrzynska and Broniarczyk think he will use his power of veto to block the bills, preventing them from becoming law.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s now been more than two years since Odysseas Vlachodimos made his one and only appearance for Newcastle United, but he remains on the books at St James’ Park.

The Greek goalkeeper was signed from Nottingham Forest by Eddie Howe in the summer of 2024 as part of the arrangement which saw Elliot Anderson going the other way, with his solitary outing coming against AFC Wimbledon during the triumphant Carabao Cup campaign.

The 32-year-old has been on loan at Sevilla since August of last year, having had the deal extended for another season, and he’s been a regular starter with the LaLiga outfit.

In an interview with El Desmarque, Vlachodimos was asked if he’d like to join the Andalusian club outright from Newcastle.

It has been revealed that he replied emphatically, and with a smile on his face: “I’ve already stated it, yes. I really like the club and Spanish football. The club is like a family. I get along very well with all the players and coaches.

Now, 30 years later, Mitre has reimagined the legendary ball, bringing it back with a modern twist.

The fresh Ultimax Pro 30th Anniversary Ball merges the classic design with cutting-edge technology, celebrating its iconic status while setting a new standard for the next generation.

While the ball retains the familiar 6-panel construction, the classic white, blue, and red colourway, and the unmistakable crown logo, itâs been upgraded with advanced features. The interior also sees improvements, with Hyperfoam cushioning now enhanced for cleaner strikes and even more power.

To mark the milestone, Mitre has introduced the "The Next In Line" campaign, spotlighting the latest wave of football talent carrying on their family legacies.

The campaign features rising stars such as Raphaella Wright-Phillips, granddaughter of Arsenal icon Ian Wright, Ruben Butt, son of Manchester United legend Nicky Butt, and Jacob Fowler, whose father is Liverpoolâs own Robbie Fowler.

The trio, each in vintage 95/96 kits, embody the connection between the past and the future â just as the fresh Ultimax Pro does itself.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott indicated Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that 'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off.

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

'No chance,' noted Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'.

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline.

'People who played for the club mentioned 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured), in cell lines that should not be able to produce them.
  • Recent findings suggest that A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines.
  • Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured), in cell lines that should not be able to produce them. Credit: Dr Mark J. Winter/Science Photo Library.

Recent findings suggest that A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines. In these studies, particular proteins show up in imaging experiments, even though the cells do not have the gene necessary to make them.

Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.

“This problem will not go away,” notes Thierry Soussi, a cancer geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden, who notes that there are several other examples of the matter in now-retracted papers that were not included in the sleuth’s analysis. “This is only the tip of a gigantic iceberg.”.

Cell lines are groups of cells derived from a single origin cell and cultured for use in experiments. Some cancer cell lines have been genetically modified with mutations and deletions — often to remove genes that usually control cell division. This means that the cultures continually divide and grow, giving researchers the chance to study tumour progression and test potential treatments.

Industry observers note that the MCF-7 cell line is one of these. It lacks the gene for caspase-3 protein, which is involved in cell death. In 2009, researchers warned1 that some studies that report working with MCF-7 have mysteriously observed caspase-3 expression in western blots, an imaging technique that identifies proteins based on their molecular weight.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody.

In the most recent analysis, published as a preprint on 21 October to the data repository Zenodo2, Sholto David, a sleuth based in Arbroath, UK, finds that this problem persists and extends to other cell lines.

David compiled a list of 20 commonly used cell lines with genetic mutations or deletions that leave cells unable to express specific proteins. He then scoured the literature using Google text and image searches to identify examples of western-blot images that unexpectedly identify these proteins. He also searched a collection of 140,000 articles that he had previously downloaded and screened for image-integrity issues and other problems, most of which were biomedicine papers.

It has been revealed that he found 230 reports of phantom proteins across 221 papers published since 2004. The most common errors were observations of caspase-3 expression in the MCF-7 cell line, affecting 49 papers; expression of the cell-death protein BAX in the Jurkat cell line in 47 papers; and expression of the signalling protein STAT3 in the PC-3 cell line in 35 papers.

David suggests several explanations for these impossible protein-expression patterns. They might be the result of honest errors: researchers could have misidentified the cell lines or contaminated them with others. Or the antibodies used to identify proteins in the western-blot experiments could have been non-specific and bound to another protein with the same molecular weight. In fact, David indicates that he stumbled across the anomalous proteins while working on a project that flagged hundreds of studies that used the wrong antibodies in experiments.

Another possibility is that some of the papers are the product of papermills, companies that fabricate and sell scientific manuscripts. David says that some papers in the cache contain the hallmarks of being produced by such outfits, including duplicated images or text templates that are similar to other papers. The proportion of the papers that fall into this category is not clear, he says.

Nature has contacted several authors of papers containing anomalies to ask for comment, but none responded.

Science sleuths raise concerns about scores of bioengineering papers.

The 26-year-old remains one of the world’s most feared strikers, so any genuine availability would immediately trigger interest from Europe’s biggest clubs.

Liverpool are among those watching developments, although Real Madrid, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain would provide formidable competition.

According to Fichajes, Man City could consider selling Haaland for around €150million in the summer of 2027.

Liverpool are monitoring the situation alongside Real Madrid, Barcelona and PSG, with uncertainty surrounding City’s Premier League financial case continuing to fuel speculation about the striker’s future.

Haaland is also contracted until 2034 and does not have a release clause, leaving City in an extremely strong negotiating position.

A recent report also named Liverpool as the leading Premier League contender if City eventually sanction a sale.

From Liverpool’s perspective, there is little debate about the footballing appeal.

Haaland would provide a devastating focal point, combining elite movement, physical power and a goalscoring record few forwards can match.

But spending around €150m on one player would reshape Liverpool’s entire transfer strategy. The Reds already have significant investment tied up in their attack, so a deal of this scale could require major departures before it becomes realistic.

According to recent reports, real Madrid may also represent the biggest threat. Haaland has long been linked with the Spanish giants, and competing financially with Madrid, Barcelona and PSG would be difficult.

Liverpool should still remain involved. Opportunities to sign a striker of Haaland’s quality almost never emerge. If City genuinely open negotiations, Liverpool would be foolish not to explore the possibility.

For now, though, this remains an opportunity to monitor rather than a transfer that is close to happening.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that is Germany's economy back on the up?
  • According to recent reports, at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen.
  • The mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

According to recent reports, at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I said here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

The mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.

Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.

In a recent development, "[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location.".

Recent findings suggest that german Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

Industry observers note that merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz stated in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

It has been revealed that given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz remarked when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.

The economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

Industry observers note that "The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," noted Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending.".

The chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that.".

But these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

According to recent reports, at the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.

"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she said.

The government is at the moment in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in new debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.

The economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

According to recent reports, germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that however, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," stated Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.

Sources indicate that the so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, said the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.

"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer mentioned.

Sources indicate that according to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an issue in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz noted there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a tech giant can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.

According to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

If the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it said in the report. "New technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop.".

But innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

New evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

The intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a new study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association revealed that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.

This article was originally written in German.

'The Road to Wembley', hosted at the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art in collaboration with VERSUS, offered supporters an immersive, documentary-style retelling of the Magpiesâ cup success.

The launch event included a panel featuring curators Ewen Spencer and Jimmy Turrell, alongside Newcastle legend Rob Lee, before celebrations spilled into the night with a DJ set.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kevin De Bruyne had plenty to say ahead of his return to the Etihad Stadium with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday night, criticising reporters at his press conference for creating an ‘unpleasant situation’ for him and his wife, while also commenting on Manchester City being found guilty of over 100 charges relating to the Premier League’s financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that de Bruyne is back in Manchester and is due to take on Manchester City in the Champions League league phase at 20.00 GMT on Tuesday night. This will be De Bruyne’s second visit to the Etihad since joining Napoli, having lost 2-0 against his former side in the league phase last September.

De Bruyne, who has been linked with a move away from Napoli in recent weeks, sat down for his pre-match press conference on Monday evening.

De Bruyne began with an assessment of his own game and remarked that he feels that he is having a decent season on an individual level.

Industry observers note that analysing the role he plays for Napoli, he stated: “I’ve played in a lot of different roles in my career, I’ve changed positions a lot of times. Your role can always change in football.

According to recent reports, “I play based on the things I feel on the pitch, where I see the space, where I believe I am most dangerous. I feel like I’m playing well this year, it doesn’t matter where on the pitch that is.”.

Sources indicate that de Bruyne was then asked about his own future and the recent suggestions that he could leave Napoli in January, if not when his contract expires at the end of the season. Recent reports claim that PSV Eindhoven have made an offer for his services.

His wife was also the subject of a recent magazine interview in Belgium, in which she discussed the possibility of one day returning to the family home in Belgian Limburg, but De Bruyne feels that this was completely misinterpreted back in Italy.

“To be honest I’m pretty annoyed. If you go and read the article, which none of you have read, you will understand what she noted. I was away in Belgium and then a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions came to my wife and my family.

“I saw photos of my house [in the press], which I don’t think is okay but it is what it is. I know that journalists in Italy have created this situation and I don’t know why. You do not know my life, It’s not been nice for my wife or my family. It is what it is.”.

In a recent development, pressed again on whether he could leave Napoli in the near future, De Bruyne remarked: “There’s not a lot I can say at this point. I’ve plated at 400% so far. I’m not 20 years old anymore, I’m almost 36, so there are lots of things to consider.

It has been revealed that “Right now, there’s not a lot to say. I’m playing well, I’m trying to help the team to do well. There have been lots of challenges this year and a lot of things have happened.”.

Recent findings suggest that on the prospect of facing Manchester City, with whom De Bruyne won six Premier League titles as well as the 2022-23 Champions League, he stated: “I understand the way that City play, obviously. I know Enzo [Maresca], I know the way he likes to play football and how he positions his players.

epa10675973 Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola (L) speaks to assistant manager Enzo Maresca during a training session on the UEFA Champions League media day at the City Football Academy in Manchester, Britain, 06 June 2023. Manchester City will play Inter Milan in the UEFA Champions League final at the Ataturk Olympic Stadium in Istanbul on 10 June 2023. EPA-EFE/ADAM VAUGHAN“I think you always have to have courage to play football, you cannot only go long and play for duels.”.

Members of the British press were keen to hear De Bruyne’s reaction to Manchester City being found guilty of over 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.

He mentioned: “This is my club, I love the owners. I’ve nothing but affection for this club and that will never change.

“Of course in life there are rules, everybody plays on the limit I would say and for me I play in between the white lines and I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players, so for me that is the thing that I value most and even later on in my career I think the most vital is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

“I’ve given my all and that is not going to change in my mind I don’t think. Other people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played but everybody has their own opinion I guess.”.

The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star eyes new lucrative deal with clubs circling, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1122 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:17 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.
  • De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:17 EST, 23 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Industry observers note that williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old stated he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Similarities are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No.10 position.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

Recent findings suggest that he does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

Recent findings suggest that his brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a newly introduced talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

According to recent reports, the Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' mentioned De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Currently under contract until 2028, the 18-year-old has rival clubs circling if Spurs cannot pin him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

Williams-Barnett is under contract until 2028 but is understood to be closing in on a lucrative latest deal to tie him down because others have been circling.

It has been revealed that it is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping complications but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

In a recent development, although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' noted De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

According to recent reports, there was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'Mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

Recent findings suggest that the pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Moyes is unsure as to whether or not Everton will appeal the red card shown to James Tarkowski in the 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Monday night.

The centre-back received his marching orders in the 40th minute for a studs-up challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk, with Craig Pawson upgrading his decision from a yellow card after viewing the pitchside VAR monitor.

The 34-year-old is set to face a three-match suspension, starting with the Merseyside derby next Sunday and also ruling out of the subsequent games against Aston Villa and Fulham.

When speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Moyes was asked whether Everton would appeal Tarkowski’s red card, to which he simply replied: “Don’t know yet.”.

The Toffees manager later admitted that he’d revised his original stance on the incident, saying (via Liverpool Echo): “My first feeling at the time was I didn’t think it was red because I thought James easily got to the ball before Yehor Yarmolyuk.

“I could have said that the Brentford player was a bit late in getting there, but after seeing it again I can see that Tarky’s boot is a bit higher than I like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.”.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The rights or wrongs of the red card decision will be debated throughout the week, but Tarkowski didn’t do his Everton teammates any favours with his lunge on Yarmolyuk, especially when they were already 2-0 down and just about still in the contest at that point.

His suspension for the next three games (pending an appeal) also comes as a blow to the Toffees, particularly ahead of the derby next Sunday, when he won’t get the chance to replicate his stoppage-time equaliser from the memorable Goodison Park clash two seasons ago.

Moyes now has just two centre-backs available for the game against Liverpool in Jarrad Branthwaite and Michael Keane, so the Scot will be living on his nerves this week that neither of those succumb to injury in the coming days.

That the Everton boss felt the red card was justified seems telling, and Tarkowski will be bitterly disappointed with his rush of blood to the head last night.

The Toffees’ task of recording a first derby win since April 2024 has become notably harder without the experienced defender, unless they lodge (and win) an appeal, which right now seems improbable.

#163100. AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1409 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1409 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW.
  • Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium. He and his classmates have already been using artificial intelligence-enabled tools, or AI, for the last two and a half years.

Recent findings suggest that "I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW. Jakob isn't his real name, because he doesn't want to publicly admit he and many others of his age use AI to do their homework.

Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.

In science, this is called "cognitive outsourcing." Basically, the required thinking is shifted to another device, whether that's a calculator, notepad or a large language model (LLM) like ChatGPT.

There's a difference with AI, though. A notepad or calculator can take over a step or two but rarely the whole thought process. That's not the same for an LLM, which can handle the entire problem-solving process.

Jakob admitted he's also had an AI help him with his homework. "But only when I was really stuck," he insisted. And he's also aware that it can become a problem when AI does all your homework. "The students who get good grades tend not to do that," he explained.

Franziska Müller has been a German teacher for several decades and is right now teaching senior classes at a gymnasium. Her name has also been changed for privacy reasons.

"They can't even think for themselves anymore," she told DW, complaining about some of her classes.

According to recent reports, even in ordinary classes, some of the students type their questions into their tablets or phones, asking for AI assistance. And should they be called upon in class, she knows that they're reading out the answers that the AI has prepared for them and hoping nobody notices.

Industry observers note that müller believes students these days are less able to comprehend text. "Because they read less and let AI summarize almost everything for them," she said.

Several studies have reached very similar conclusions.

Sources indicate that that includes the latest PISA (Program for International Student Assessment) study from September. PISA, which is run by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, regularly evaluates the abilities of 15-year-old students around the world.

"Students who report using AI chatbots get lower scores in science, on average, than those who don't use AI," Andreas Schleicher, the OECD director for education and skills, wrote in his report in October. "This includes using AI to summarize texts they had to read, conduct preliminary research on a upcoming topic, or draft texts for writing assignments.".

In a recent development, with participants from more than 90 countries, PISA is considered the largest international comparative study of 15-year-olds worldwide. This year, German 15-year-olds posted their lowest PISA scores in the 25-year history of the study.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"The connections are complex and depend heavily on how generative AI is used, but the central insight is simple: Just as we don't get fit by watching sports but by doing sports ourselves, learning doesn't come from consuming content, but from the mind's productive cognitive engagement with upcoming material," Schleicher explained.

Put simply, those who don't exercise their brains risk becoming less intelligent.

US think tank, the Brookings Institution, has already argued that the risks of using AI in education outweigh the benefits.

Its own research, which included young participants from around the world, speaks of students losing "fundamental cognitive and durable skills as they increasingly rely on AI to perform learning's intellectual work," as well as the decline of critical thinking, memory, perseverance and independent judgment.

But what can be done against the power of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini and Meta AI?

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has banned the use of AI in public schools up to the eighth grade for the 2026 and 2027 school years — so that's up to about the age of 14 or 15.

In a recent development, not everyone agrees this is the right thing to do. Julian Hinn, who teaches German to students aged between 15 and 18 in Germany, stated class members can still use AI apps on their mobile phones. "And anyone who thinks they won't use it at home is ignoring reality," Hinn told DW.

Germany's annual JIM study, which tracks teenagers' media use and device ownership, supports that view.

91% of young people surveyed in Germany, between the ages of 12 and 19, stated that they use at least one AI application. The study also reports that 74% use AI for homework and learning.

Industry observers note that the last JIM study actually dates back to 2024 so those percentages might be even higher now. Data on AI use in Asia, Latin America and the US from the Brookings study show similarly high figures.

German politicians have recognized the problem. Although education in Germany is the responsibility of the individual federal states, the so-called Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, or KMK, has been issuing statements on the use of AI since 2024.

The KMK's statements have been rather vague though, saying only that students should be enabled to engage with AI in a critical, reflective and responsible manner.

Teachers and students alike are aware that AI can be a powerful support in the classroom.

"The AIs simply explain things much better than textbooks," noted Jakob, adding that he'll often get an AI to explain basic concepts to him.

Sometimes teachers can't respond like an AI, Hinn conceded. "The AI ​​can respond much better to the language and needs of the students.".

That's why he thinks it's important to include AI in classes, starting from the 10th grade when students are around 15 or 16. Hinn doesn't think it should be introduced before that, when children's basic skills are still being developed.

According to recent reports, in more senior classes, Hinn will encourage his students to question the AI critically. "We look at the quality of the solutions," he explained.

According to recent reports, german teacher Müller has also integrated some use of AI into her lessons for older students. But in some aspects of the class, she also bans it altogether so that her students can focus on thinking for themselves.

"I understand very well that it's tempting to use AI," she remarked.

There are also other problems with AI in education. According to the Brookings study, students with basic skills can use AI to deepen their learning and progress faster.

Recent findings suggest that but for children with gaps in their knowledge, they tend to adopt AI's errors, outsource their thinking and then fall even further behind. In this way, AI can exacerbate preexisting inequalities.

The PISA study notes that children from more affluent backgrounds often have a better start, and AI can widen that gap.

This is called the Matthew effect — the name comes from the biblical verse Matthew 25:29, "for unto everyone that hath shall be given." It basically means that early success in learning leads to better progress in the future, while early struggles equal a growing lag over time.

In the age of AI, teachers have become more motivated to challenge students to think independently and to consider their own personal autonomy.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hinn, who also supervises the school newspaper, stated: "I always tell everyone, you can use AI but the feeling of having written an article with your own pen is spectacular.".

Both teachers also stress the idea of personal autonomy and responsibility. They believe this affects the students, especially because when they sit exams, they aren't allowed to use any aids or AI. And if they aren't able to solve their own problems, they will fail.

It's during exam time that the students really find out if they can solve those math, English or science problems by themselves.

Müller said one of her students recently confessed they were upset after a poor exam result. "He felt he simply couldn't think for himself anymore because of AI," she said.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Massimiliano Allegri maintained his stance that Tuesday’s Champions League match against Manchester City will not be the be-all and end-all for Napoli, even if they have only picked up three points from four games in the competition so far and are at risk of missing out on qualification for the knock-out rounds.

Allegri sat down for his pre-match press conference on Monday evening, ahead of Tuesday night’s test against Man City in the Champions League league phase, which kicks off at the Etihad Stadium at 20.00 GMT.

Earlier on Monday, City head coach Enzo Maresca had joked that ‘We’re always good at complaining in Italy’ after being told what Allegri had said about Tuesday’s fixture over the weekend.

Allegri had made it clear that Man City were the obvious favourites and that Napoli’s qualification for the Champions League knock-out rounds depends on their final three league phase fixture, and not this one against Man City.

Industry observers note that at his press conference on Monday evening, Allegri clarified: “I just said that it won’t be decisive, because mathematically, even if we win tomorrow, six points won’t be enough to qualify. So, I will only believe that we’ve qualified once we have achieved it on the final matchday. It’s a matter of numbers. We definitely need at least three wins, mathematically.”.

In a recent development, looking ahead to Tuesday’s game, Allegri added: “We know how difficult it will be, because we’re playing against one of the strongest teams in Europe, even after 10 years of winning in the Premier League and a Champions League victory and with so many changes of players. It’s a new group, but they have extraordinary qualities.

“It’s a Champions League match against one of the favourites to go on and win it. As always, we’ll need great technique when we have the ball and when we don’t. We’ll have to do our best to create the conditions to counter Man City.”.

Sources indicate that allegri went on to provide an injury upgrade on his squad. Napoli are without 11 first team players for their trip to Manchester, the latest being Italy international Antonio Vergara, who is out for the rest of the calendar year and beyond with a thigh injury he suffered over the weekend.

“We have some players who are recovering,” Allegri confirmed. “Di Lorenzo and Badiashile will definitely be available for Lecce, Favasuli and Marianucci are not on the Champions League squad list, then we’ve also lost Meret and Vergara, but that’s part of the game.

“I’ve seen the injury numbers across Europe. Lots of teams have injured players. We have to make do with what we’ve got and know that it will take even more desire to win it as a team.

“From Wednesday onwards, we will be preparing for our next game in the league, where we are a bit behind because we could have picked up a few more points.”.

Asked how he motivates his team ahead of such a big game like tomorrow’s against Manchester City, Allegri mentioned: “These games prepare themselves in terms of motivation. If we aren’t motivated, we clearly don’t understand where we are playing.

“That mentioned, there will be objective difficulties against a team with such great technique and physicality and we will have to play well. We have to defend as a team when we don’t have the ball and not make the mistakes we made against Porto, where we got a bit scrambled trying to recover the result.”.

Allegri has been in management for over 20 years, but has never coached outside of his native Italy. Asked if he would like to take on a job abroad at some stage, Allegri noted: “It’s always intrigued me, but the choices I’ve made have been different and I have no regrets.

“In fact, I’m very happy because I’ve been very lucky. I’ve poached some massive teams in Italy: Juventus, Milan and Napoli. Let’s not forget Cagliari, where I started, either.

“Coming to play in these sorts of stadiums and facing these sorts of teams is always great. We do this job to play in these types of matches and to prove that we are one of the best. Tomorrow will be a great game. The clear goal is to progress, regardless of what happens tomorrow.

“Of course, getting a result would be wonderful, especially after the win against Torino, but at the same time, if we do lose, we haven’t compromised anything.”.

Kevin De Bruyne was sat next to Allegri for the pre-match press conference. The Belgian was asked questions on his future with the club and Allegri was then asked for his thoughts.

Industry observers note that “Kevin’s already said it, I haven’t spoken to him because we’re in the middle of the season,” said Allegri. “We will have the Coppa Italia on December 16 and then when we have the Christmas break from December 21, the club will make its assessments.

“We want to fix the squad. It also depends on the will of the players, whether they want to stay or leave. But we need to focus on the goal, getting to December 20.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling new era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool.

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathematicians.
  • In a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field.
  • The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California, tech giant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathematicians. Credit: James Brittain/Getty.

In a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field. But on the same day as the Anthropic claim, a separate study claiming to have proven the Riemann also emerged — and this one is entirely human written.

The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California, tech giant. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote, referring to Anthropic’s large language model (LLM).

“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” states number theorist James Maynard, a winner of the Fields Medal — mathematics’ most prestigious prize — at the University of Oxford, UK.

Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics.

Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics.

Hours later, Ravi Vakil, a mathematician at Stanford University in California, posted a rival preprint to Alpöge’s online, in what Vakil called a “hurried announcement” of a proof that “is all human, with no AI”. The preprint was written by Alessandro Maria Masullo, a mathematician who received his PhD at Stanford in 2020 under the supervision of number theorist Brian Conrad. “The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people,” Vakil wrote. “Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”.

The confirmation of either or both solutions would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Bernhard Riemann, the German mathematician who was born 200 years ago this September and who formulated the problem, which addresses the distribution of prime numbers, in the mid-1800s.

Industry observers note that the Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has its scientific headquarters in Oxford, UK , at the turn of the twenty-first century. The institute offers a US$1 million prize to anyone who devises a solution to one of the problems, which are considered some of the most challenging in the field. Mathematicians using AI tools announced earlier this year that they had solved another Millennium problem, related to the Navier-Stokes equation.

Recent findings suggest that the problem has to do with the ‘Riemann ζ function’ (ζ is the Greek letter zeta), which encodes the randomness properties of the prime numbers. Riemann discovered that the distribution of primes is encoded in the ζ function’s ‘zeroes’. These are points, denoted by z, on a plane satisfying the equation ζ(z) = 0.

Sources indicate that riemann conjectured that apart from some obvious but uninteresting cases, all such solutions had to lie on a certain vertical line in the plane. If this were true, he showed, it would imply that prime numbers are scattered among all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as random as it could be.

In a recent development, alpöge’s four-page document includes a sketch of the proof. But Andrew Granville, a number theorist at the University of Montreal in Canada, says that Alpöge should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up before making the announcement, which came just days after Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO). The IPO initially valued the company at US$1.5 trillion, but the company’s valuation dropped on 19 November.

“What he released is garbled,” Granville indicates of Alpöge’s document. Granville cites the downturn in the company’s stock value as the reason for the timing of the proof’s release.

“There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false,” Alpöge wrote in the document.

Anthropic did not respond immediately to Nature’s request for comment.

In a recent development, tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University who collaborated with Alpöge on a separate project regarding the Navier-Stokes equation, says that Alpöge deserves a lot of credit for developing techniques to produce mathematical results using LLMs. “Levent himself built this amazing set-up to do math.” He adds that Alpöge, who is himself a number theorist on leave from Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been working relentlessly for months on this and other problems, hardly ever getting any sleep.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI.

“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct,” Maynard indicates of the Alpöge announcement, even though it is now in the form of incomprehensible code in the Lean programming language.

Sources indicate that “At the moment, it apparently is crazily complicated. It’s going to take a long time for mathematicians to digest,” claims Buckmaster. Maynard agrees, but he adds: “Assuming we do get the corresponding understanding, this will surely be viewed as one of the absolute pinnacles of mathematical results.”.

Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find new forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

It has been revealed that countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," said Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

In a recent development, she indicates it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it highlights it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She says it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF plans and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott said.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national plans to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no new commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Industry observers note that kumar claims more countries could announce similar looks just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

Sources indicate that the nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

According to recent reports, the roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

It has been revealed that kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any big announcements about fossil fuels.

Global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald demonstrates that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing upcoming reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

One issue Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar said, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".
